Chapter 6: Embracing Frustration—Navigating the Emotional Side of Learning.
You know that feeling when you’re making great progress at something new, and then, suddenly, it feels like you hit a wall? That’s what a lot of learners experience—a stretch where improvement slows down, and frustration starts to set in. It’s such a common part of the learning curve, people even call it the “valley of disappointment.”
In the beginning, everything feels exciting. Every little win gives you a boost. But after that first burst of progress, reality kicks in—and you realize that moving forward is going to take patience and persistence.
Here’s something you might not hear enough: the emotional side of learning is just as important as the technical stuff. We all face frustration, self-doubt, even boredom. These feelings can drain your motivation if you let them. But what if you saw them as a normal part of the process, not as signs you’re failing?
Imagine learning as a hike up a hill. At first, it’s steep and maybe a bit tough, but you see progress fast. Then the path flattens out. You’re still moving forward, but it doesn’t always feel like it.
So, how do you get through this phase? Here are a few things that really help:
First, acknowledge frustration as a sign of growth. If you feel stuck, it probably means you’re stretching into new territory.
Next, try breaking your practice into smaller, more manageable chunks. When your motivation dips, short, focused sessions are much easier to stick with.
And don’t forget to celebrate the small wins. Even the tiniest improvements can reignite your enthusiasm and remind you that you’re still making progress.
Take someone learning to draw, for example. Maybe their sketches still don’t look the way they hoped, and it’s discouraging. But if they look back at their very first attempt and compare it to today, the progress stands out—even if perfection still feels far away. That simple shift in perspective can turn frustration into fuel, and keep the momentum going.
Building up emotional resilience is actually part of learning itself. When you accept that plateaus and setbacks are just part of the journey, you’ll be able to push through tough moments—and come out even stronger on the other side.
